name: Blocking Chips
description: You are given a tree, consisting of $$$n$$$ vertices. There are $$$k$$$ chips, placed in vertices $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k$$$. All $$$a_i$$$ are distinct. Vertices $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k$$$ are colored black initially. The remaining vertices are white. You are going to play a game where you perform some moves (possibly, zero). On the $$$i$$$-th move ($$$1$$$-indexed) you are going to move the $$$((i - 1) \bmod k + 1)$$$-st chip from its current vertex to an adjacent white vertex and color that vertex black . So, if $$$k=3$$$, you move chip $$$1$$$ on move $$$1$$$, chip $$$2$$$ on move $$$2$$$, chip $$$3$$$ on move $$$3$$$, chip $$$1$$$ on move $$$4$$$, chip $$$2$$$ on move $$$5$$$ and so on. If there is no adjacent white vertex, then the game ends. What's the maximum number of moves you can perform?
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of testcases. The first line of each testcase contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of vertices of the tree. Each of the next $$$n - 1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$v$$$ and $$$u$$$ ($$$1 \le v, u \le n$$$) — the descriptions of the edges. The given edges form a tree. The next line contains a single integer $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le k \le n$$$) — the number of chips. The next line contains $$$k$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the vertices with the chips. All $$$a_i$$$ are distinct. The sum of $$$n$$$ over all testcases doesn't exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each testcase, print a single integer — the maximum number of moves you can perform.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1795F — Blocking Chips [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
